claim: update() evaluates getLoginPredicate on the org-aware wrapper returned by getById, whose isEnabled() is false when the org (or realm orgs) is disabled; hiding/link-only/un-publicizing such an IDP then skips login-cache invalidation, and the stale cached ID resurfaces on the login page once the org is re-enabled because the bean only re-checks isEnabled().
body:
## [ISSUE] Login-cache invalidation on update evaluates the org-aware wrapper, so edits to IDPs of a disabled organization never invalidate the cache

**Severity:** MEDIUM — hidden, link-only or non-public organization IDPs can reappear on the login page after the organization is re-enabled

### The Problem

```java
IdentityProviderModel idpById = getById(model.getInternalId());   // line 91
registerIDPInvalidation(idpById);
registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(idpById, model);             // line 93
```

When the ORGANIZATION feature is on, `getById` returns `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel(...)` (line 141). That wrapper overrides `isEnabled()` so it returns `false` when the linked organization is disabled, or when organizations are disabled for the realm (`provider.isEnabled()`, line 441). `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` then runs `getLoginPredicate()` on this wrapper. The `ENABLED` filter makes `original` look like a non-login IDP even though the stored row is still `enabled=true` and is still in the cached `ORG_ONLY`/`ALL` ID sets.

### Theory / Proof

1. The cached ID sets come from `idpDelegate.getForLogin`, which is a JPA query on the raw `ENABLED`/`LINK_ONLY`/`HIDE_ON_LOGIN`/`BROKER_PUBLIC` columns (`IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:165-184`). It knows nothing about whether the organization is enabled, so an IDP of a disabled org stays in the cached set.
2. Organization enable/disable does not invalidate the login keys. The design relies on the wrapper's `isEnabled()` at read time. That is why `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` now re-checks only `idp.isEnabled()` (lines 75 and 80).
3. Admin update path: `IdentityProviderResource.updateIdpFromRep` builds `updated` with `RepresentationToModel.toModel`, which is a plain model. If the admin sets `hideOnLogin=true`, `linkOnly=true`, or removes `BROKER_PUBLIC`, `getLoginPredicate().test(updated)` is `false`.
4. Both predicates are `false`, so the first early return (line 405) fires and no login key is invalidated.

### What happens today vs. what will break

Scenario: org O has public IDP X, and the `ALL`/`ORG_ONLY` login caches have been populated. An admin disables O, or turns off organizations on the realm, and then sets X to "hide on login" (or link-only, or not public). The login caches keep X's ID. When O is re-enabled, `getForLogin(ALL, ...)` returns X from the cache. `getById(X)` returns a fresh model with `hideOnLogin=true`, but the bean filters only on `isEnabled()`, so X is shown on the login page. That contradicts the admin's setting, and for `BROKER_PUBLIC` it exposes a non-public org broker. The cache only recovers on another invalidating change or eviction.

### Research

`getByOrganization` in this same class avoids the problem because its key is invalidated through `isInvalid(orgId)`. Keycloak's other cache layers (e.g. `RealmCacheSession`) decide invalidation from the stored state, not from a decorated view.

### Recommendation

Evaluate the predicate against the persisted model, not the org-aware wrapper:

```java
@Override
public void update(IdentityProviderModel model) {
    IdentityProviderModel idpById = getById(model.getInternalId());
    registerIDPInvalidation(idpById);
    // use the raw stored model so org-enabled state does not mask login-relevant changes
    registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(idpDelegate.getById(model.getInternalId()), model);
    idpDelegate.update(model);
}
```

`model` can itself be a wrapper (e.g. from `JpaOrganizationProvider.addIdentityProvider`), so also compare the raw login flags (`enabled`, `linkOnly`, `hideOnLogin`, `BROKER_PUBLIC`, `organizationId`) directly, or invalidate whenever any of them differ. Defence in depth: have the bean apply the full `getLoginPredicate()` to cached results instead of only `isEnabled()`.

claim: The login cache stores one entry per fetch mode with a search key per organizationId, so in ALL/ORG_ONLY modes it grows linearly with orgs (duplicating realm-level IDs) and is fully copied and re-added on each new org lookup.
